The algebra notes are split across these pages:

- The [Equalities, Inequalities and Minimizers](algebra-basics.qmd) page:
  equalities, inequalities, powers, square roots and absolute values,
  minima and maxima, and global and local minimizers.
- The [Convexity, Infimum and Sums](algebra-sums.qmd) page:
  convex functions, the infimum and supremum,
  sums, products and quotients, summation notation, limits of sums, and notational shorthands.
- The [Polynomials, Affine Functions and Series](algebra-polynomials.qmd) page:
  polynomials, affine and linear functions of one variable,
  limits of [sequences](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-sequence), and [series](algebra-polynomials.qmd#def-infinite-sum).
- The [Exponentials and Logarithms](algebra-exponentials.qmd) page:
  exponentials and logarithms.
- The [Trigonometry](algebra-trigonometry.qmd) page:
  cosine and sine on the unit circle, and the identities later pages use.
- The [Complex Numbers](algebra-complex.qmd) page:
  complex numbers and their arithmetic.

A link to a section, theorem or definition on this page from before the split
goes on to the page that now holds it.

# Further reading {#sec-further-reading}

- @abramson2021algebra
  is a free online textbook on algebra and trigonometry.
  It covers equations, inequalities, polynomials, exponentials, logarithms, and trigonometry,
  which overlap with the algebra in these notes.
- @rudin1976principles
  develops the real numbers, including the least upper bound property
  behind the infimum and supremum.
